references.text: Horeb is also called the mountain of God, the same mountain where Moses met God at the burning bush.
Aaron met Moses at the mountain of God, showing that this was a well-known meeting place in the wilderness.
The background to Jethro's relationship with Moses as father-in-law, and Moses' marriage to Zipporah and their sons.
Moses took his wife and sons with him when he went to Egypt; now they return to him.
The context explaining that Jethro had taken in Zipporah and her two sons after Moses sent them back.
Hobab, son of Reuel (Jethro), Moses' father-in-law, is mentioned in connection with the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.
Heber the Kenite, who was a descendant of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, shows the family line from Jethro.
Verse 12 completes the story begun in verse 5 by showing Jethro's offering and fellowship with Israel's leaders.
Both verses illustrate Jethro's central role as father-in-law and supporter of Moses before and after the exodus from Egypt.
This verse broadens the perspective by showing that Jethro's descendants (the Kenites) continued to play a role in Israel's settlement in Canaan.
Verse 27 concludes the same story begun in verse 5, demonstrating the completeness of Jethro's visit.
